correctness.rationale: The order-two min-square kernel is exactly the squared pair difference minus the reflection-odd midpoint-separation kernel, each with coefficient 1/2. The pairwise sum-of-squares identity yields the exact sample representation for all nonconstant vectors, while reflection symmetry forces the population target to zero. Finite fourth moments justify the Hoeffding projection CLT and denominator consistency. The centered uniform law has an exact cubic conditional projection and normalized limiting variance one seventh; a folded-normal calculation gives the Gaussian reference integral and its numerically evaluated constant. The bundled checker ran 18,443 exact or high-precision assertions. General proofs, not finite experiments, establish the quantified claims.

value.rationale: The gap is about identifiability and power, not a textbook sign normalization: compressing a valid pointwise Stein characterization into this signed scalar contrast makes an infinite class of fixed non-Gaussian symmetric alternatives indistinguishable in population. An exact reflection-odd sample formula and an explicit uniform distribution with approximately 0.000563 limiting rejection at nominal 0.05 give a concrete test-design warning. This does not imply failures of nonnegative L2 or fitted-location variants.
